A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same sigmoid-attention study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered between versions.

before.justification: V1 reports original vision, language-modeling, speech-recognition, synthetic-task, and GPU-timing experiments in Section 5 and Appendices F–G.

after.justification: V2 retains these experiments and adds empirical Jacobian measurements, normalization ablations, 7B language-model results, and normalization-overhead benchmarks.

M1.justification: V2 introduces hybrid normalization as an additional stabilization strategy, normalizing attention outputs before residual addition. Its language-model and ASR variants can replace earlier bias or normalization requirements (Sections 5.5, G.3.3, G.4.2, G.6). This substantially extends the proposed training procedure, although the sigmoid attention formula and FlashSigmoid algorithms remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The ImageNet, C4/RedPajama, English language-model benchmarks, LibriSpeech/TED-LIUM, and synthetic summation and pair-repeat coverage is retained. The added 7B experiments expand model scale, not datasets or tasks.

E2.justification: Hybrid-normalized SoftmaxAttn variants are added as language-model comparators in Tables 3 and 11. Existing comparison families remain. The original 4K RoPE softmax baseline's accuracy results move from Table 3 to Appendix Table 11 rather than being removed.

E3.justification: V2 adds 7B models at 4096-token context, controlled normalization/bias/positional-encoding configurations, and exact autograd Jacobian-norm evaluation across sequence lengths. New timing experiments compare FlashSigmoid plus LayerNorm against FlashAttention2 with affine parameters enabled or disabled. These substantially extend experimental settings without establishing reruns of retained experiments.

E4.justification: New Figure 7 directly examines empirical versus theoretical regularity, with and without hybrid normalization. Appendix G.3.3 adds language-model normalization ablations, G.4.2 adds ASR hybrid-normalization/QK-norm/LayerScale ablations, and G.6 measures normalization overhead. These investigate important stability and efficiency questions absent from v1.

E5.justification: New Figure 7 explicitly reports ten trials per sequence length and displays variability. Existing timing uncertainty and synthetic-task quartile reporting are retained. There is no stated increase in repetitions for the earlier experiments.

E6.justification: V2 retains the original 1B benchmark accuracies and adds hybrid-normalized 4K results: sigmoid versus softmax averages are 50.2 versus 49.4 at 1B and 59.6 versus 59.0 at 7B (Table 3). The new 7B step times are 3.4 versus 3.85 seconds. Additional Jacobian, ASR, and normalization-overhead results are reported; these are new configurations, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Section 3.3/Table 1 revises the operation accounting: softmax changes from 3c nctx to 5c nctx, matching sigmoid, and the reported difference becomes zero. The universal-approximation theorem, Lipschitz bound, and Appendix C–E proofs remain unchanged. Section 4 nevertheless retains the earlier statement that sigmoid is theoretically slower.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's four contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about universal approximation, regularity, FlashSigmoid efficiency, and cross-domain performance parity. The new normalization and larger-model evidence supports these existing headline claims.

C2.justification: The unresolved long-context language-model limitation in v1 becomes a conditional remedy using hybrid normalization in v2, with its added computational cost acknowledged in Appendix A and quantified in G.6. Section 3.2 also newly distinguishes worst-case Lipschitz bounds from practical average behavior, while the new analyses interpret normalization's role in stability.

D1.justification: Table 10 newly specifies RMSNorm and pre-norm for the existing 1B recipe. Appendices G.3.3–G.6 document hybrid-normalization placement, affine-parameter choices, and ASR component substitutions; Table 17 consolidates practitioner settings. These improve implementation guidance, although a dedicated detailed 7B training configuration is not supplied.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations connecting the analysis to attention dynamics and documenting LayerScale, LayerNorm, RMSNorm, and hybrid-normalization precedents, including Grok-1 and Praxis. The principal positioning against prior attention alternatives in Section 6 remains unchanged; expanded author names in the bibliography are formatting changes.

P1.justification: Section 5.5 is rewritten around the expanded language-model evidence, and new regularity discussion, a normalization subsection, and a practitioner's guide improve the narrative. Most existing prose and the overall section organization remain intact, with localized edits and bibliography-style changes.

P2.justification: V2 adds Figure 7 and Tables 11, 17, and 18, expands Figure 2 with 7B curves, and restructures or extends Tables 3 and 16. These are localized display additions; most existing figures and tables retain their content with renumbering, resizing, or relocation.

improvement.justification: V1 explicitly leaves the 1B/4096-token performance gap unresolved. V2 supplies a tested normalization remedy, matched softmax controls, and 7B validation, substantially strengthening the practical case for sigmoid attention. Empirical regularity checks and normalization-overhead benchmarks also improve evidential support and qualify efficiency benefits. Extra normalization costs are disclosed; incomplete 7B configuration details and the residual FLOP-text inconsistency do not outweigh these gains.
